# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (GTM context) |

## JD Complement
This is a scale-design role at the intersection of enterprise AI, external delivery capacity, and technical trust. Anthropic needs partners to help customers move from interest in frontier models to durable, governed use in real workflows.

The core tension is expansion without erosion: broaden enterprise reach through an ecosystem while preserving the quality, safety posture, and architectural consistency associated with Anthropic.

A strong leader in this seat would turn complex field learning into repeatable methods, helping partners deliver credible outcomes without requiring Anthropic specialists to remain embedded in every implementation.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco. Claude is its principal product family, supported by an identity centered on AI systems that are reliable, interpretable, and steerable.

The company combines frontier-model research with an increasingly broad enterprise product surface. Claude serves business users, developers, and organizations building AI-enabled applications, creating multiple paths into an account.

Anthropic’s operating model requires close connection between research values, product decisions, commercial growth, and real-world implementation. That makes deployment quality an extension of company credibility, not only a services
concern.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s safety-centered positioning creates a higher bar for how enterprise adoption is supported. Buyers and partners need practical guidance that connects model capability with security, governance, user change, and measurable value.

The company must balance reusable patterns with customer-specific needs. Too much standardization can limit relevance; too much customization can make ecosystem growth expensive, inconsistent, and difficult to govern.

A partnerships architecture function can help establish the middle ground: clear technical principles, reusable solution patterns, escalation paths, and disciplined feedback loops that improve both partner readiness and product
understanding.

The key strategic question is whether partners can become trusted long-term delivery extensions while Anthropic retains clarity over technical standards, product boundaries, and responsible-use expectations.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
The meaningful stakeholder environment is cross-functional and outcome-oriented:
- Partnerships and commercial teams require reliable technical engagement models that improve partner confidence and account execution.
- Security, enterprise, and customer-facing groups need implementation patterns that remain consistent across customer and partner handoffs.
- Partner technical leaders need practical learning paths, solution assets, and clear signals about when to engage Anthropic specialists.
- Customer technology, security, and business owners need a coherent path from AI experimentation to governed operational use.

The role is likely most effective when it can translate across commercial urgency, architecture detail, customer risk concerns, and partner delivery economics.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic presents Claude as both an enterprise offering and a platform for applications and agents. The architecture conversation therefore extends beyond model access into integration design, evaluation, observability, permissions,
workflow design, and operational controls.

Enterprise materials emphasize security, compliance, and support for business teams and developers. This suggests that technical adoption must connect end-user experience with engineering implementation rather than treating them as
independent motions.

Deployment guidance covers setup, organizational launch, enablement, and scaled usage. That is a useful signal: sustained value depends on behavior change and operating discipline, not only successful provisioning.

Claude Code administration also links AI deployment to software-development environments, access management, and developer adoption. Technical partners will need patterns that account for both business transformation and engineering
productivity.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic describes a partner ecosystem across cloud, technology, and services organizations. This points to a model in which partners contribute infrastructure choices, implementation capacity, industry context, and complementary
capabilities.

A durable ecosystem motion should include:
- Technical discovery that leads to viable, governable solution designs rather than generic demonstrations.
- Partner learning programs tied to delivery readiness and observable customer outcomes.
- Reusable industry and workflow patterns built from recurring customer needs.
- Clear collaboration models for high-stakes opportunities requiring both partner ownership and Anthropic expertise.
- Feedback mechanisms that separate systemic product gaps from isolated implementation issues.
- Quality signals that assess adoption, operational stability, and customer value after initial launch.

The central test is whether partners can create enduring customer success independently while remaining aligned with Anthropic’s technical and trust standards.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s enterprise materials increasingly address the full adoption lifecycle, including administration, organizational rollout, learning, and expansion. This raises the execution standard for partners participating in customer
delivery.

Platform messaging around applications and managed agent infrastructure broadens the technical surface area that partners must understand. Customers will need guidance spanning model use, application architecture, controls, and lifecycle
operations.

Competition also increases the need for clarity. Enterprise buyers can access AI capabilities through many vendors and channels; Anthropic’s differentiation depends on making Claude practical to adopt while sustaining confidence in
reliability and responsible deployment.

The near-term opportunity is to convert field complexity into partner-ready operating mechanisms before inconsistent delivery patterns become entrenched.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise AI architecture leadership across partner and customer environments.
- Repeatable implementation patterns derived from complex technical engagements.
- Ecosystem enablement across cloud, services, and technology partners.
- Moving organizations from early experimentation toward durable, governed adoption.
- Translation between external delivery teams and internal product or engineering groups.
- Security-conscious architecture, evaluation discipline, and responsible AI practices.
- Structured customer insight loops that improve product readiness and delivery quality.
- Technical team leadership in fast-changing, ambiguous operating conditions.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s ecosystem spans multiple partner categories, making consistency in technical execution strategically important.
- The enterprise adoption lifecycle indicates focus on value realization after initial access is enabled.
- Agent-oriented platform capabilities create demand for stronger partner architecture methods and reusable solution assets.
- Anthropic’s public-benefit identity makes trustworthy implementation part of its market position.
- The leadership challenge is scaling partner capability while keeping architecture quality, customer outcomes, and field learning high.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The job description and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume and proof graph.

Location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience.
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position.
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, Anthropic expects all staff to be in one of its offices at least 25% of the time. Some roles may require more time in office.
Visa sponsorship: Anthropic says it sponsors visas but cannot successfully sponsor every role and candidate.
"
}

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (GTM context) |

## JD Complement
This is a scale-design role at the intersection of enterprise AI, external delivery capacity, and technical trust. Anthropic needs partners to help customers move from interest in frontier models to durable, governed use in real workflows.

The core tension is expansion without erosion: broaden enterprise reach through an ecosystem while preserving the quality, safety posture, and architectural consistency associated with Anthropic.

A strong leader in this seat would turn complex field learning into repeatable methods, helping partners deliver credible outcomes without requiring Anthropic specialists to remain embedded in every implementation.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco. Claude is its principal product family, supported by an identity centered on AI systems that are reliable, interpretable, and steerable.

The company combines frontier-model research with an increasingly broad enterprise product surface. Claude serves business users, developers, and organizations building AI-enabled applications, creating multiple paths into an account.

Anthropic’s operating model requires close connection between research values, product decisions, commercial growth, and real-world implementation. That makes deployment quality an extension of company credibility, not only a services
concern.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s safety-centered positioning creates a higher bar for how enterprise adoption is supported. Buyers and partners need practical guidance that connects model capability with security, governance, user change, and measurable value.

The company must balance reusable patterns with customer-specific needs. Too much standardization can limit relevance; too much customization can make ecosystem growth expensive, inconsistent, and difficult to govern.

A partnerships architecture function can help establish the middle ground: clear technical principles, reusable solution patterns, escalation paths, and disciplined feedback loops that improve both partner readiness and product
understanding.

The key strategic question is whether partners can become trusted long-term delivery extensions while Anthropic retains clarity over technical standards, product boundaries, and responsible-use expectations.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
The meaningful stakeholder environment is cross-functional and outcome-oriented:
- Partnerships and commercial teams require reliable technical engagement models that improve partner confidence and account execution.
- Security, enterprise, and customer-facing groups need implementation patterns that remain consistent across customer and partner handoffs.
- Partner technical leaders need practical learning paths, solution assets, and clear signals about when to engage Anthropic specialists.
- Customer technology, security, and business owners need a coherent path from AI experimentation to governed operational use.

The role is likely most effective when it can translate across commercial urgency, architecture detail, customer risk concerns, and partner delivery economics.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic presents Claude as both an enterprise offering and a platform for applications and agents. The architecture conversation therefore extends beyond model access into integration design, evaluation, observability, permissions,
workflow design, and operational controls.

Enterprise materials emphasize security, compliance, and support for business teams and developers. This suggests that technical adoption must connect end-user experience with engineering implementation rather than treating them as
independent motions.

Deployment guidance covers setup, organizational launch, enablement, and scaled usage. That is a useful signal: sustained value depends on behavior change and operating discipline, not only successful provisioning.

Claude Code administration also links AI deployment to software-development environments, access management, and developer adoption. Technical partners will need patterns that account for both business transformation and engineering
productivity.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic describes a partner ecosystem across cloud, technology, and services organizations. This points to a model in which partners contribute infrastructure choices, implementation capacity, industry context, and complementary
capabilities.

A durable ecosystem motion should include:
- Technical discovery that leads to viable, governable solution designs rather than generic demonstrations.
- Partner learning programs tied to delivery readiness and observable customer outcomes.
- Reusable industry and workflow patterns built from recurring customer needs.
- Clear collaboration models for high-stakes opportunities requiring both partner ownership and Anthropic expertise.
- Feedback mechanisms that separate systemic product gaps from isolated implementation issues.
- Quality signals that assess adoption, operational stability, and customer value after initial launch.

The central test is whether partners can create enduring customer success independently while remaining aligned with Anthropic’s technical and trust standards.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s enterprise materials increasingly address the full adoption lifecycle, including administration, organizational rollout, learning, and expansion. This raises the execution standard for partners participating in customer
delivery.

Platform messaging around applications and managed agent infrastructure broadens the technical surface area that partners must understand. Customers will need guidance spanning model use, application architecture, controls, and lifecycle
operations.

Competition also increases the need for clarity. Enterprise buyers can access AI capabilities through many vendors and channels; Anthropic’s differentiation depends on making Claude practical to adopt while sustaining confidence in
reliability and responsible deployment.

The near-term opportunity is to convert field complexity into partner-ready operating mechanisms before inconsistent delivery patterns become entrenched.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise AI architecture leadership across partner and customer environments.
- Repeatable implementation patterns derived from complex technical engagements.
- Ecosystem enablement across cloud, services, and technology partners.
- Moving organizations from early experimentation toward durable, governed adoption.
- Translation between external delivery teams and internal product or engineering groups.
- Security-conscious architecture, evaluation discipline, and responsible AI practices.
- Structured customer insight loops that improve product readiness and delivery quality.
- Technical team leadership in fast-changing, ambiguous operating conditions.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s ecosystem spans multiple partner categories, making consistency in technical execution strategically important.
- The enterprise adoption lifecycle indicates focus on value realization after initial access is enabled.
- Agent-oriented platform capabilities create demand for stronger partner architecture methods and reusable solution assets.
- Anthropic’s public-benefit identity makes trustworthy implementation part of its market position.
- The leadership challenge is scaling partner capability while keeping architecture quality, customer outcomes, and field learning high.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The job description and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume and proof graph.
